candidates.evidence: MOCI Circular No. 4 of 2025 makes registration on the MOCI Inspections Portal mandatory for DPMS, statutory auditors, fund service providers and companies (https://www.moci.gov.qa/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Circular-No-4-of-2025-3.pdf; DPMS page https://www.moci.gov.qa/en/about-the-ministry/anti-money-laundering-and-terrorism-financing/supervised-entities/dealers-in-precious-metals-or-stones-dpms/). Law 20/2019, Decision 48/2020, Circular 7/2024. Same buyer and duty as K02. Circular date unverified.
candidates.known_note: Same buyer group and core duty (AML compliance for gold/jewellery dealers); the circular adds a portal-registration trigger, not a new buyer.
candidates.name: DPMS/jewellery AML Inspections Portal registration and compliance pack (MOCI Circular 4 of 2025)

candidates.buyer: Private sewage-tanker owners and haulage contractors with Ashghal tanker permits
candidates.existing: Competitor search (English) found no named approved vendor or fleet software. Device is tied to Ashghal's own system with Ashghal-issued SIM, so a third-party platform has little to do. Not checked in Arabic.
candidates.name: Sewage-tanker owner/contractor compliance and tracker-registration tool (Ashghal 4G/5G device rule)
candidates.trigger: Ashghal requires a tracking device linked to its system for entry to treatment plants. 2G/3G devices discontinued 31 Dec 2025. Permit applications and renewals need proof of a working device. Application by email 'Private Tanker Configuration'.
candidates.unchecked: Tanker count, permit renewal cycle, certificate/inspection tracking, any fines, whether a private vendor ecosystem exists, Arabic competitor search.

candidates.buyer: Employers and manpower/recruitment firms hiring in professions the Ministry designates
candidates.evidence: https://www.klgates.com/thought-leadership/Qatar-Introduces-Significant-Amendments-to-the-Labour-Law-9-1-2026 ; https://www.clydeco.com/en/insights/2026/07/qatar-updates-the-labour-law-what-employers-need ; https://www.middleeastbriefing.com/news/qatar-revises-work-permit-and-labour-service-fees/ (MD 32/2025 fees). Related to K03 (WPS) and K05.
candidates.existing: Not searched yet; list of professions unknown, so no product shape.
candidates.name: Regulated-profession accreditation and recruitment-licence tracker under Labour Law 9/2026 (Article 23 bis 1)
candidates.trigger: Law 9/2026 (in force 25 June 2026) lets the Ministry designate professions that need accredited training, exams and a licence. Implementing decisions not yet issued. Stronger WPS suspension powers.
candidates.unchecked: The designated professions list and effective dates, who carries the duty, whether Metrash or a Ministry portal handles it. Revisit when the decisions are published.

candidates.buyer: Licensed limousine companies and app-based passenger transport firms, and sponsors of public-licence drivers
candidates.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
candidates.existing: None found. Fleet and Karwa software was not searched specifically. Enforcement count is small and no recurring report to the regulator was found.
candidates.name: Passenger-transport/limousine small operator compliance register (MOT Decision 13/2024)
candidates.trigger: MOT inspection campaigns under Law 8/2019 and Decision 13/2024: 32 violations Q1 2026, 66 in Q1 2025. MOI Traffic Law 19/2007 Arts 30-31 require a public driving licence sponsored by an operator.
candidates.unchecked: Number of licensed operators, what records inspectors demand, school-bus rules, whether MOT's portal already holds the data.

candidates.buyer: Private nurseries (about 179 in 2023), mostly owner-run
candidates.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
candidates.existing: Not searched yet in Arabic; generic nursery-management apps probably exist (unverified).
candidates.name: Nursery licence, staffing-qualification and inspection readiness tool (MOEHE 2024 decisions)
candidates.trigger: MOEHE decisions of July 2024: three nursery types, staff qualification requirements, premises conditions, QR1,000 licence/renewal fee, annual renewal under Law 1/2014, six-month grace period.
candidates.unchecked: Official text of the 2024 decisions, what inspectors check, existing nursery software, the Arabic competitor search required for a 3-point score.

candidates.buyer: Licensed domestic recruitment offices (325 in 2019, count now unverified)
candidates.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
candidates.existing: None searched.
candidates.known_note: Same buyer and duty as the placement and guarantee tracker.
candidates.name: Household recruitment office compliance pack (price cap, guarantee refund, new contract forms)
candidates.trigger: Ministry inspections check the new contract forms, the maximum recruitment price decision and the extended 9-month guarantee; 10 offices were closed in April 2024.

candidates.buyer: Falcon breeders and traders
candidates.existing: Filing is made through the Ministry's own platform, so little room for third-party software.
candidates.name: Falcon breeder/owner CITES permit and passport filing
candidates.trigger: Supreme Council for Environment Decision 6/2026 sets a falcon passport system with electronic ID. The Ministry's falcons platform had 24,000 requests by Sept 2026.
candidates.unchecked: Whether intermediaries or agents file for owners, the fees, the number of breeders.

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K04/K05. Searches found no 2025-26 decree for recruitment offices. Known context: 9-month guarantee (2022), recruitment price cap, new contract forms checked by inspectors, 10 offices closed in April 2024 (al-sharq.com/article/02/04/2024). Contract authorisation runs through Metrash2.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: No municipal scrap-dealer register found. Only a 2013 Peninsula piece saying scrap and battery handlers need an environment licence, and a 2025 MOCI land-allocation scheme for recycling factories in Al Afja. No recurring small-dealer reporting duty confirmed.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No second-hand or pawnbroker regime found. Not covered by the DNFBP list in the results. Pawnbroking is probably not a licensed activity in Qatar (unverified).

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K02. DPMS are DNFBPs under Law 20/2019 for cash of QR50,000 or more. MOCI Circular 4 of 2025 requires DPMS to register on the MOCI Inspections Portal (see candidate C1). Law 4/2022 caps cash in jewellery sales at QR50,000.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No dismantler licensing or deregistration rule found. Only the abandoned-vehicle committee's 2025 report (7,144 vehicles cleared) and a university ELV study. Nothing actionable.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: No current trader or transport permit text found. Only old Livestock Dept clinic and market-entry information. Ministry of Municipality is the likely regulator (unverified).

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: No dedicated search; the livestock search returned nothing on abattoirs or butchers. Ministry of Municipality food-safety rules not checked.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Qatar has a negligible beekeeping sector in a desert climate and no registration regime surfaced. No search spent.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Veterinary practice law requires a ministry licence for practice and clinics, and clinics must be Qatari-owned with at least 51% Qatari share (FAOLEX text, old). Vet medicine registration is by ministry with the health ministry. No current software-relevant recurring report found.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Law 1/1988 as amended 1995 and Environment Minister Decision 24/2014 set well-drilling licences valid 3 years. No recurring reporting found. Weak.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Ashghal sewage-tanker permits require a tracking device linked to Ashghal's system. 2G/3G devices were discontinued on 31 Dec 2025 in favour of 4G/5G. Digital landfill/dump permits exist via the Ministry of Municipality. No MECC waste manifest found. See candidate C2.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: No Qatari statutory inspection-interval rule or approved-inspector list surfaced; results were job ads and Bahrain rules. Inspection firms (Bureau Veritas, TUV) are present. Unverified for Qatar.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Water is supplied by Kahramaa. No small-water-system operator duty found. No search spent.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Pest-control firms need a MOCI commercial licence and follow Ministry of Public Health guidance (directory sources only). No official register or applicator reporting duty found.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Labour Law amendments Law 9/2026 (in force 25 June 2026) add Article 23 bis 1 for professions needing accredited training, exams and a licence, plus stronger Wage Protection System enforcement. Implementing decisions were still awaited. MD 32/2025 sets recruitment-licence fees at QR2,000. See candidate C3.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Burial is state-run (Municipality/Awqaf) with an MOI Humanitarian Services Office at Hamad. No private funeral-licence regime found. Nothing actionable.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: RACA (Law 15/2014) regulates charities and fundraising permits. Private associations are governed by Decree-Law 21/2020. No recurring-report detail found. The buyer group is small and mostly large state-linked charities. Weak.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: MOT inspects limousine and app-based passenger companies under Law 8/2019 and Decision 13/2024 (32 violations in Q1 2026; 66 in Q1 2025). MOI requires a public driving licence for taxi, limousine and bus drivers (Aug 2026). See candidate C4.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Exchange houses are licensed under Law 4/1982 and supervised by QCB (Law 13/2012). No small-exchange reporting product found; the sector is small. Street vendors are not a recognised category.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: MOEHE July 2024 decisions created three nursery types, staff qualification rules and QR1,000 licence/renewal fees (about 179 nurseries in 2023). Driving schools are inspected by MOI Traffic (rules are old). Falcon passports and CITES go through a government platform (Decision 6/2026). Small food producers are covered by K01. See candidate C5.

candidates.buyer: Small landlords who own several units (often Qatari families), real estate brokerage offices and property managers
candidates.category: 31. Real estate lease law 8 of 2026 (also 28. real estate brokers)
candidates.existing: Competitor search (Arabic) found no Qatar-specific landlord or lease-registration software; results were Dubai (Ejari, Dubai REST) and a generic landlager.com Qatar compliance page. The state's own online registration channel was not confirmed.
candidates.known_note: Same broker buyers as K02 but a different duty (lease registration, not AML).
candidates.name: Lease Registration and Renewal Kit for Small Landlords, Brokers and Property Managers (Law 8 of 2026)
candidates.trigger: Law 8 of 2026 amends Law 4 of 2008 on real estate leasing. Effective 3 Sept 2026. Landlords must register each lease with the Real Estate Lease Registration Office (Ministry of Municipality) for a flat QAR 250 per unit, and the registration number (RNR) is needed for Kahramaa utility connection. Disputes must now go through the Rental Disputes Committee before any lawsuit. The general registration deadline is unverified (an older guide says 30 or 60 days).
candidates.trigger_note: One-off cliff on 3 Sept 2026 has already passed; the repeating part is annual renewal and new leases.
candidates.unchecked: General registration deadline, penalties after the grace period, whether the state e-service is free and easy (Metrash2 or MoM portal), how many multi-unit small landlords exist, and whether landlords delegate to brokers.

candidates.buyer: Small private employers with a few Qatari employees
candidates.existing: Generic payroll vendors (Ramco, Mercans) cover it as a feature. GRSIA's own portal was not checked. No competitor search was run (budget used).
candidates.known_note: Adjacent to the WPS payroll validator, but a different authority and duty. The generic payroll rejection (K06) may apply.
candidates.name: GRSIA Pension Contribution and Annual Return Helper for Employers with Qatari Staff
candidates.trigger: Social Insurance Law 1 of 2022 and Cabinet Resolution 3 of 2025: register Qatari employees within 30 days (one vendor says 14 days), pay 14% employer and 7% employee contributions by the 5th of each month, update data within 30 days, and submit an annual January return. Penalties conflict between sources: 2% on arrears, an extra 10%, or criminal exposure.
candidates.unchecked: GRSIA portal capabilities, how many small firms employ Qataris, the competitor search, and the real penalty schedule.

candidates.buyer: Wholly Qatari or GCC-owned micro companies, home-licence holders, charities and associations
candidates.category: 33. Tax return filing for all CR holders
candidates.existing: Accounting and audit firms and tax advisers. No competitor search was run (budget used).
candidates.known_note: Different duty from UBO declarations. Close to generic accounting, which is out of scope, so the wedge is thin.
candidates.name: Annual Tax Return Filing Service for Tax-Exempt Qatari/GCC-Owned Micro Firms and Associations (Dhareeba)
candidates.trigger: The GTA requires all CR, trade-licence and home-licence holders, including exempt entities and some charities, to file annually on Dhareeba. The 2025 deadline was 30 Apr 2026, extended to 30 Jun 2026. The 2026 window was not found.
candidates.unchecked: Whether the return for exempt entities is simple enough for a self-serve tool, penalties for non-filing, competitor search, and the number of home-licence holders.

candidates.buyer: Small restaurants, cafeterias, groceries, bakeries and caterers
candidates.existing: Competitor search: no Qatar-specific tracker found; only the individual-user Nar'aakom app and the Hukoomi expiry check, plus a generic non-Qatar food-handler tracker. Spreadsheets are the likely substitute.
candidates.known_note: Same food-business buyer as K01 but a different duty (staff cards, not product registration).
candidates.name: Staff Health-Card and Food-Handler Permit Tracker for Small Food Businesses
candidates.trigger: The employer is legally responsible for valid health cards and training for all staff. Food-handler permits last 3 years and medical certificates are renewed yearly (sources conflict). MoM closures of 7-30 days are common (12 closures in Jan 2026).
candidates.unchecked: Official validity periods, whether MoPH offers an employer bulk-check portal, and willingness to pay. Close to a generic document-expiry tool.

candidates.buyer: Small hotels, hotel apartments and guest houses
candidates.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals
candidates.existing: PMS vendors such as Kwentra already generate the Qatar police report.
candidates.name: Hotel and Guest-House Guest Report and Licence Compliance Tool
candidates.trigger: Hotels submit guest ID reports to the Ministry of Interior (source: a vendor help page, so unverified as a legal requirement). The tourism licence lasts 5 years, and classification fees apply.
candidates.unchecked: Whether small guest houses use a PMS, the MoI channel, and how often the report is due.

candidates.buyer: Individual owners of holiday homes and Airbnb-style units
candidates.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals
candidates.existing: Free state portal. Sources are 2021-2022, so the current status is unverified.
candidates.name: Holiday Home Licence and Platform Compliance Pack for Individual Owners
candidates.trigger: Qatar Tourism holiday-home licence is free and valid 5 years, inspected, with a 75% guest-satisfaction condition. Platforms deactivate listings without a licence number (Airbnb since 23 Sept 2022). Penalty for unlicensed renting reported as up to 2 years in prison and/or QAR 200,000.
candidates.unchecked: Current rules, number of licences now, and whether owners hire agents.

candidates.buyer: Small workshops, clinics, labs and industrial users that handle chemicals or generate hazardous or healthcare waste
candidates.existing: Not checked. A free state e-system exists.
candidates.name: Hazardous Chemicals and Waste Permit and Manifest Helper (MoECC digital system)
candidates.trigger: Environment Protection Law 30 of 2002 (articles 22-41) and healthcare waste instruction 8 of 2006. The MoECC e-system launched in 2024 has 23 services and 1,850+ registered companies, so the duty is already digital.
candidates.unchecked: Which small businesses must register, record-keeping and manifest duties, how painful the e-system is, and consultants already doing it.

candidates.buyer: Small employers and household employers with non-Qatari staff
candidates.existing: Insurers and brokers handle enrolment. No competitor search was run.
candidates.known_note: Overlaps the household-employer buyer of K04.
candidates.name: Employer Mandatory Health Insurance Enrolment Tracker (Law 22 of 2021)
candidates.trigger: Employers must buy MoPH-registered private cover for non-Qatari employees, spouse and up to 3 children; cover must be active before the work permit is issued. The QAR 30,000 fine figure is from a broker guide only.
candidates.unchecked: Official penalties, how enrolment is checked, and insurer portals.

candidates.buyer: Private pharmacies
candidates.existing: Unknown. Pharmacy management systems likely cover it.
candidates.name: Private Pharmacy Narcotic and Psychotropic Register
candidates.trigger: Narcotics and psychotropics are controlled under Law 9 of 1987 and require special licences. Register and reporting duties were not found.
candidates.unchecked: Whether pharmacies keep paper registers, MoPH reporting channel, and incumbents.

candidates.buyer: Small private clinics and polyclinics
candidates.existing: Not checked.
candidates.name: Private Clinic Facility-Licence Compliance Pack (medical director, minimum practitioner counts)
candidates.trigger: MoPH closes facilities that operate without a medical director, below the minimum practitioner headcount, or before licence approval (Peninsula, Aug 2025). Practitioner licences require CPD for renewal.
candidates.unchecked: The facility licence renewal cycle, inspection checklists, and incumbents.

candidates.buyer: Real estate brokers, gold and jewellery dealers, auditors, TCSPs
candidates.category: 28. Notaries, brokers and professionals with AML duties
candidates.existing: Not checked.
candidates.known_note: Same buyer group and same core duty (DNFBP AML). The circular is new evidence for K02, not a new idea.
candidates.name: MOCI DNFBP Compliance Officer Registration and Self-Assessment (Circular 4 of 2025)
candidates.trigger: Register a Compliance Officer and Deputy on the MOCI Inspections Portal, upload CR, IDs, CVs and appointment forms, and complete the Self-Assessment Questionnaire. Shared contact details between the two roles are not allowed without approval.

candidates.buyer: Licensed security-guard companies (Qatari-owned)
candidates.existing: Not checked. Sources are a study-guide site and old news, so the details are unverified.
candidates.name: Security Company Licensing Compliance (MoI Law 19 of 2009; Resolutions 7 and 93 of 2021)
candidates.trigger: 3-year licence, guard training and clearance duties, and MoI action against unlicensed firms.
candidates.unchecked: Number of licensed firms, periodic reporting to MoI, and whether the duty falls on the firms or their clients.

candidates.buyer: Small shops, restaurants, warehouses and clinics
candidates.evidence: No reliable source found (search returned unrelated or UAE material).
candidates.existing: Not checked.
candidates.name: Civil Defence Fire-Safety Certificate Tracker
candidates.trigger: Civil Defence Law 19 of 2009 is cited by an unofficial guide only. The renewal regime was not confirmed.
candidates.unchecked: Everything: law, renewal cycle, inspection and maintenance-contract rule.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: WOQOD holds the sole concession for fuel/LPG distribution to commercial, industrial and government customers, and is the only LPG cylinder distributor (Shafaf). Small private distributors are essentially absent, and the buyer is a monopoly. A 1998 resolution on gas cylinder circulation (FAOLEX) exists but I could not confirm it is in force. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Not a producing country and no commodity-trader regime found. Food import registration is already covered by K01 (Watheq). No dedicated search run.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: No search run. Not tested against a register; Qatar has no meaningful credit-union or savings-group sector, and charities and associations fall under group A (17). Marked not applicable from background knowledge, not from a source.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: MoPH licenses facilities and practitioners, and closes facilities for having no medical director or too few practitioners (Peninsula, Aug 2025). Employer-paid private insurance has been mandatory for non-Qatari workers since Law 22 of 2021 took effect in May 2022. Found nothing on claims-billing mechanics or a small-clinic duty that software could solve. Weak or unverified leads only (C06, C11).

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: The MoPH Pharmacy and Drug Control Department regulates; narcotics and psychotropics fall under Law 9 of 1987, and a new electronic traveller permit system lists 140 controlled medicines (Aug 2026). I could not find private-pharmacy register rules. MoECC's chemical and hazardous-waste e-system has 23 e-services and 1,850+ registered companies (C07). Pharmacy registers are unverified (C10).

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Security companies are licensed by MoI under Law 19 of 2009 (Qatari ownership required, 3-year licence) and MoI Resolution 7 of 2021 as amended by Resolution 93 of 2021. MoI has pursued 13 unlicensed firms. I found no SME-scale duty beyond licensing. Related WPS/manpower ideas are K03, K04 and K05.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers
coverage.found: No contractor classification or registration regime found. Ashghal prequalifies project by project, with Qatari-ownership rules (documents dated 2013-2015). Small Municipality works tenders are under QAR 200,000 on Monaqasat. Nothing found for a quiet-business wedge.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with AML reports
coverage.found: MOCI supervises DNFBPs (brokers, precious metals and stones dealers, auditors, TCSPs). MOCI Circular 4 of 2025 requires a Compliance Officer and Deputy to be registered on the Inspections Portal, with a Self-Assessment Questionnaire. Same buyer and duty as K02. Law 8 of 2026 (lease registration) gives brokers and landlords a new duty (C01).

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals
coverage.found: Qatar Tourism holiday-home licence: free, valid 5 years, e-services portal, inspection, 75% guest-satisfaction condition, platforms must show the licence number since September 2022. Hotel tourism licence is valid 5 years. Guest reports to MoI exist but are served by PMS vendors such as Kwentra (C03, C04).

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules
coverage.found: Imported-goods Certificate of Conformity is already rejected (K08). Food registration is K01. No new traceability regime found. No dedicated search run.

coverage.category: 31. Real estate lease law 8 of 2026 (country-specific)
coverage.found: Law 8 of 2026 amends Law 4 of 2008; effective 3 Sept 2026; flat QAR 250 registration fee; settlement fee for violations cut from QAR 5,000 to QAR 1,000; Rental Disputes Settlement Committee is now mandatory before suing (C01).

coverage.category: 32. Pension contributions for Qatari employees (GRSIA, Law 1 of 2022; Cabinet Resolution 3 of 2025)
coverage.found: Employers with Qatari staff must register employees and pay 14% employer plus 7% employee contributions by the 5th of the following month, with a January annual data submission (C02). Sources conflict on penalties.

coverage.category: 33. Tax return filing for all CR holders, including exempt Qatari/GCC-owned firms and charities (Dhareeba)
coverage.found: The GTA requires every entity with a CR, trade licence or home licence to file, including exempt ones. The 2025 deadline was extended from 30 Apr to 30 Jun 2026 (C08).

coverage.category: 34. Food-business licensing and health cards (MoPH/MoM)
coverage.found: MoM closed 12 food establishments in Jan 2026 and ran 154,000+ inspections in Q2 2025. Food-handler permits last 3 years and health certificates are renewed annually (sources conflict). The employer is responsible. Official Nar'aakom app and Hukoomi check single cards only (C09).

coverage.category: 35. Hazardous chemicals and waste e-system (MoECC)
coverage.found: The digital system launched in 2024 has 23 e-services, 57,699 applications, and 1,850+ registered companies. Environment Protection Law 30 of 2002 and healthcare waste instruction 8 of 2006 apply (C07). Rules for small sites not confirmed.

coverage.category: 36. CCTV and security systems (MoI Security Systems Dept)
coverage.found: MoI publishes a list of 162 licensed or approved surveillance-camera companies (Apr 2026). I found no mandate for businesses to install cameras and no deadline (C05).

coverage.category: 37. Civil Defence fire-safety certificates
coverage.found: Searches returned nothing reliable. Civil Defence Law 19 of 2009 is unverified and no renewal regime was confirmed. Marked unverified (C12).

coverage.category: 38. Employer-mandated health insurance (Law 22 of 2021)
coverage.found: Employers must buy MoPH-registered private cover for non-Qatari employees and families. Fines of up to QAR 30,000 come from a single broker guide only (C06).

coverage.found: No candidate found. Slaughter is channelled to state-designated abattoirs: Widam Food runs the central abattoir and the automated Al Wakra facility, and Aswaq (Hassad) manages the central markets. Sources: https://www.qatar-tribune.com/article/181046/FIRSTPAGE/Countrys-biggest-automated-abattoir-begins-operations and https://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/27/05/2026/ministry-of-municipality-urges-public-to-use-designated-abattoirs-for-eid-sacrifices. The Ministry of Municipality provides veterinarians who examine animals before and after slaughter, and it urges the public to use designated abattoirs for Eid and to avoid roaming butchers (May 2026). Retail butcheries are inspected by municipal health-control sections under Law No. 8 of 1990 on human food control (cited in Peninsula and Gulf Times reporting). Meat samples go to the MOPH Central Laboratory. Food handlers need MOPH health certificates (unverified: the 3-year permit and annual medical details come from an unofficial study guide). Imported meat is governed by MOPH halal import guidance (2022 version) and Watheq registration, which is already covered by K01 and K08. I found no butcher-specific recurring register or report that the shop files with an authority: the duties are inspections, health cards and a one-off licence, not a recurring filing. The Qatar-specific butchery licence checklist, fees and activity code were not found (no official Ministry of Municipality or Single Window page surfaced; the Ministry of Municipality site was not fetched). A search for butcher software found no Qatar-specific vendor; only generic POS and traceability tools (e.g. Toast, Kern) showed up. Net: the category is thin, as there are few independent small abattoirs, and the duty falls mostly on state-run or Widam-run facilities.

result.reason: The duty is real. Ashghal has barred tankers without a tracking device from its treatment plants since 1 Aug 2022. It also refuses to accept or renew tanker permits without proof of a working device. The 4G/5G update ends 2G/3G devices on 31 Dec 2025 (Qatar Tribune). Ashghal supplies the SIM and links the device to its own system. Registration is one email form to avltankersupport@ashghal.gov.qa, so little is left for third-party software. The article states no fines. The only penalty is loss of plant access and permit renewal. I found no named vendor or fleet software. An Arabic search found no approved-installer list. I did not find a tanker count or the permit renewal cycle. The market is probably small, and the duty is one-off hardware rather than a recurring workflow. Score stays 3.

The duty is real but thin. MoEHE decisions (July 2024) create three nursery types, set staff qualifications and premises conditions, and set a QR1,000 licence and renewal fee with a six-month grace period. No decision numbers, inspection checklists or penalties were found. Annual renewal under Law 1/2014 was not confirmed in anything I opened. MoEHE has run a licensing platform with automatic reminders for private schools and KGs since Oct 2025, with multi-year licences and 18-month monitoring. I could not tell whether it covers nurseries. No nursery-specific compliance software turned up in Arabic or English. The market is about 179 owner-run nurseries, which is tiny. Willingness to pay is low and the state platform may overlap.

Duty is real: Law 8 of 2026 amends Law 4 of 2008, in force 3 Sept 2026. The landlord must register leases with the MoM Lease Registration Office within 2 months (existing Art. 3 rule). The fee is a flat QAR 250 per unit, and fines reach QAR 10,000 per Qatar Living and Al-Sharq summaries (penalty not seen in the Gulf Times article). The state already offers online registration and certificate printing at mme.gov.qa, so the core filing is done free by the state. No private Qatar-specific tool found, only generic landager.com. Registration happens once per lease, so frequency is low. Market size not found. The reminder and renewal angle is thin and the buyers are fragmented and informal. Low score.

The duty looks real but I could not confirm it from an official source. Only law-firm and payroll-vendor summaries describe it: 7% employee and 14% employer contributions, a QAR 100,000 monthly cap, payment by the 5th, and a January annual return. Penalties conflict between sources: 2% on arrears, an extra 10%, and criminal fines. I did not reach the GRSIA portal or the law text, so I could not check what the portal already does. Zoho Payroll has a GRSIA module, and Mercans and Ramco cover it as a payroll feature. The Qatar-specific market size was not found. The one headcount I found (176,125 citizens, 31,663 firms) is probably UAE data, so I discarded it. The niche is thin, and payroll generics and the state portal likely cover it.

The duty is real and recurring. The GTA requires all CR and trade-licence holders, including exempt Qatari/GCC-owned entities, to file annually on Dhareeba. The FY2025 deadline was 30 Apr 2026, extended to 30 Jun 2026 (Deloitte, Qatar Tribune). KPMG's 2024 alert gives a late-filing penalty of QAR 500/day, capped at QAR 180,000. I found no FY2026 window and no more recent source for the penalty. Exempt and simplified returns are a free state portal filing, and accounting firms already file them, often as tax representatives. I did not find a dedicated software competitor, but I ran no vendor-specific search. Market size and home-licence counts were not found. The wedge is thin because this is close to generic accounting, and willingness to pay is low for micro firms.
